correctness.rationale: The Poincare circumcircle center is c=(u²-a²)/(2u sinθ) and strict internal-circle containment is equivalent to the angle threshold. The polar probability follows by exact angular measure; hyperbolic area has normalized weight u/(1-u²)². The polynomial radical identity and explicit primitive J evaluate the disk integral. A weighted-average derivative proves unique optimal radius, and boundary expansion plus radial integration give the two exact asymptotic constants. Standalone independent tests of geometry, integration and limits passed; numerical experiments are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: Hyperbolic triangles need not have finite circumcenters. Quantifying the admissible set for a fixed base is a natural, model-invariant sampling question. The new evaluated intrinsic-area law, geometrically sharp inner exclusion, unique optimal disk and half-exponential rare-event exponent supply a complete parameter-resolved answer useful as a benchmark for random hyperbolic triangles. It is not simply a restatement of the deterministic two-horocycle locus.
